subject: geography
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which is the hottest and densest layer at the centre of the Earth?
questions.explain: The inner core is a solid ball of iron and nickel and is the hottest, densest layer.

questions.q: Ice cores are useful evidence for past climate because they:
options: Trap air bubbles recording past atmospheric gases and temperature
questions.explain: Air bubbles trapped in ice cores reveal past greenhouse gas levels and temperatures over thousands of years.

questions.q: Composite (stratovolcano) volcanoes are typically found at which margin?
questions.explain: Composite volcanoes with violent eruptions form at destructive margins where subduction melts crust.

questions.q: Convection currents that move tectonic plates occur in which layer?
questions.explain: Heat-driven convection currents in the semi-molten mantle drag the plates above.

questions.q: A tropical storm usually loses energy and weakens when it:
options: Moves over land or cooler water
questions.explain: Cut off from warm ocean moisture over land or cool seas, the storm loses its energy source and weakens.

questions.q: Many scientists predict climate change will make tropical storms:
options: Move towards the poles and stop
questions.explain: Warmer oceans give storms more energy, so they are expected to become more intense.

questions.q: Which is an example of an IMMEDIATE (short-term) response to a tectonic disaster?
questions.explain: Search and rescue happens in the hours and days straight after the event.

questions.q: Tropical storms are called hurricanes in the:
options: Atlantic and east Pacific (e.g. the Caribbean)
questions.explain: The same storm is a hurricane in the Atlantic/east Pacific, a typhoon in the west Pacific and a cyclone in the Indian Ocean.

questions.q: The calm, clear centre of a tropical storm is called the:
questions.explain: The eye is the calm low-pressure centre, surrounded by the violent eyewall.

questions.q: Which is a NATURAL cause of climate change?
options: Variations in the Sun's output and volcanic eruptions
questions.explain: Solar variation, orbital changes and volcanic activity are natural climate drivers.

questions.q: An example of an extreme UK weather hazard is:
options: A tropical cyclone forming over Britain
Heavy snow, flooding and winter storms
questions.explain: The UK experiences hazards such as flooding, storms, heatwaves and heavy snow.

questions.q: The point inside the Earth where an earthquake originates is called the:
questions.explain: The focus (or hypocentre) is the underground point where the earthquake starts.

questions.q: When two continental plates collide at a collision margin, the result is usually:
questions.explain: Neither continental plate subducts easily, so sediment and crust crumple upward into fold mountains.

questions.q: Tropical storms generally do NOT form right at the equator because:
options: The sea is too warm there
There is too little Coriolis effect to make them spin
questions.explain: The Coriolis effect is near zero at the equator, so storms cannot start spinning.

questions.q: Which is a method of earthquake PROTECTION rather than prediction?
questions.explain: Earthquake-resistant building design protects people, whereas monitoring is prediction.

questions.q: Which condition is REQUIRED for a tropical storm to form?
options: Sea-surface temperatures of at least about 27 degrees C
questions.explain: Tropical storms need warm ocean water of around 27 degrees C or more to provide energy.

questions.q: Why do earthquakes occur at conservative plate margins?
options: One plate melts into the mantle
Plates lock together then suddenly jolt as built-up pressure releases
New crust is created very quickly
questions.explain: Friction locks the sliding plates until stored pressure is released suddenly as an earthquake.

questions.q: The greenhouse effect becomes a problem for climate when:
options: Extra greenhouse gases trap more heat, warming the planet
questions.explain: Higher concentrations of greenhouse gases trap additional heat, enhancing warming.

questions.q: Effects of an earthquake are often worse in a LIC than a HIC mainly because:
options: LIC earthquakes are always higher magnitude
HICs sit further from plate margins
Buildings are less able to withstand shaking and emergency services are weaker
questions.explain: Poorer building quality and limited emergency resources increase impacts in LICs.

questions.q: At around 30 degrees north and south, air in the global circulation:
options: Sinks, creating high pressure and deserts
questions.explain: Sinking air at roughly 30 degrees forms high pressure and the world's hot deserts.

questions.q: Which is an example of ADAPTATION to climate change?
options: Building sea walls to cope with rising sea levels
Using solar panels instead of coal
questions.explain: Adaptation means coping with effects, such as defending coasts against higher seas.

questions.q: Which monitoring method helps PREDICT a volcanic eruption?
options: Measuring changes in gas emissions and ground bulging with seismometers
questions.explain: Rising gas output, ground swelling and small tremors warn that an eruption may be near.
